subject: physics
question_text: Define eddy flow in the case of a fluid.

mark_split.label: When it occurs, and its effect

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Very Short Answer Question 14 (printed p.106). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: eddy flow is the irregular motion in which small portions of a fluid rotate about their own axes, forming whirls called eddies; it sets in once the flow speed exceeds the critical velocity, and the eddies carry energy away from the main flow, matching NCERT Class-11 Chapter 10.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: When the flow of a fluid becomes
irregular, small portions of the fluid
rotate about their own axes, forming
whirls. Each whirl is called an eddy,
and this motion is called eddy flow.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say the flow is irregular and small portions of the fluid rotate about their own axes, forming eddies.
steps.why: Eddy flow describes what happens inside the fluid, not just a loss of streamline flow — the portions of fluid spinning about their own axes are the eddies themselves.
common_mistakes: Saying only that the flow becomes irregular, without saying portions of the fluid rotate about their own axes.
Confusing an eddy in a fluid with an eddy current in a conductor. These are different physical effects.

recall.must_convey: That eddy flow is the irregular motion in which small portions of the fluid rotate about their own axes, forming whirls called eddies.
accept: portions of the fluid rotate about their own axes
irregular motion, the fluid spins on itself
reject: it happens above the critical velocity

steps.memory_tip: Eddy flow: small parts of the fluid spin about their own axes.

steps.label: When it occurs, and its effect
steps.mark_note: Above critical velocity; carries energy away
lines: Eddy flow sets in once the speed of the
fluid exceeds the critical velocity, and
the flow is no longer streamline.
The eddies carry energy away from the
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say it sets in above the critical velocity, and the eddies carry energy away from the main flow.
steps.why: The critical velocity is the exact speed at which streamline flow breaks down, so eddy flow is what streamline flow turns into once that speed is crossed; the energy the eddies carry away is lost from the useful forward flow.
common_mistakes: Saying eddy flow occurs below the critical velocity. It occurs above it.
Leaving out that the eddies carry energy away from the main flow.

recall.must_convey: That eddy flow sets in once the speed exceeds the critical velocity, and the eddies carry energy away from the main flow.
reject: portions of the fluid rotate about their own axes

steps.memory_tip: Above the critical velocity the flow breaks into eddies, and the eddies carry energy away from the main flow.

insider_note: Both marks need a distinct idea: the first names the rotation, the second names when it happens and what it costs — energy carried away from the main flow.
